questions.q: M and R be the mass and radius of a disc. A small disc of radius $R / 3$ is removed from the bigger disc as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of remaining part of bigger disc about an axis AB passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plane of disc is $\frac{4}{x} M R^2$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Without cavity $\mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}$
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Mass of removed disc }= & \frac{\mathrm{M}}{\pi \mathrm{R}^2} \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{3}\right)^2 \pi \\ & =\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}}{9}\right)
\end{aligned}$
M.I. of removed disc $I_2=\frac{\frac{M}{9}\left(\frac{R}{3}\right)^2}{2}+\frac{M}{9} \times\left(\frac{2 R}{3}\right)^2$
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{18} \\ & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_1-\mathrm{I}_2=\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{18}=\frac{4 \mathrm{MR}^2}{9} \\ & (\mathrm{n}=9)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A thin uniform rod of length $2m$, cross sectional area $A$~and density $d$~is rotated about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to its length with angular velocity $\omega$. If value of $\omega$ in terms of its rotational kinetic energy $E$ is~$\sqrt{\dfrac{\alphaE}{Ad}}$,~then the value of $\alpha$& is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Rotational kinetic energy is given by& $E = \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$, here,~$I$~is moment of inertia of rod about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to it.

So,~$E = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{ml^{2}}{12}{ω}^{2}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{dAl^{3}}{12}{ω}^{2} \left(∵ mass = density \timesvolume\right)$

$⇒ E = $\dfrac{dA ( 2{)}^{3}}{24}{ω}^{2}

$⇒ \omega = $\sqrt{\dfrac{3E}{dA}}

Thus, the value of~$\alpha =3.

$

questions.q: If the radius of earth is reduced to three-fourth of its present value without change in its mass then value of duration of the day of earth will be ______ hours 30 minutes.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By conservation of angular momentum
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2 \\
& \left(\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{MR}^2\right) \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_1}=\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{M}\left(\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{R}\right)^2 \frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_1}=\frac{9}{16 \mathrm{~T}_2} \\
& \frac{1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{9}{16} \times \mathrm{T}_1=\frac{9}{16} \times 24 \mathrm{hr}=\frac{27}{2} \mathrm{hr}=13 \mathrm{hr} 30 \mathrm{mins} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A circular disc reaches from top to bottom of an inclined plane of length $L .$ When it slips down the plane, it takes time ${t}_{1}$. When it rolls down the plane, it takes time ${t}_{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{t2}{t1}$ is $\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}$. The value of $x$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If disk slips on inclined plane, then its acceleration,& ${a}_{1} = gsin\theta$
$L = \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2}$
$⇒ {t}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2L}{a1}} \ldots \left(i\right)$

If disk rolls on inclined plane, its acceleration,
${a}_{2} = $\dfrac{gsin\theta}{1 + \dfrac{I}{mR^{2}}}
${a}_{2} = $\dfrac{gsin\theta}{1 + \dfrac{mR^{2}}{2mR^{2}}}
${a}_{2} = $\d$dfrac{2}{3}gsin\theta
Now $L = \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2} \cdot {t}_{2}^{2}$
$⇒ {t}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2L}{a2}} \ldots \left($ii\right)$

Now,~$\dfrac{t2}{t1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{a1}{a2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$
$⇒ x = 2$

questions.q: Consider a uniform cubical box of side a on a rough floor that is to be moved by applying minimum possible force $F$ at a point $b$ above its centre of mass (see figure). If the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.4$ , the maximum possible value of $100 \times \dfrac{b}{a}$ for a box not to topple before moving is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For no toppling
$F\left(\dfrac{a}{2} + b\right) \le mg\dfrac{a}{2}$
$\mu\dfrac{a}{2} + \mub \le \dfrac{a}{2}$
$0 . 2a + 0.4b \le 0.5a$
$0.4b \le 0.3a$
$b \le \dfrac{3a}{2}$
$b \le 0.75a$ (in limiting case)
But it is not possible as $b$ can maximum be equal to $0 . 5a$
$∴ {\left(100\dfrac{b}{a}\right)}_\max = 50.00$

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about a perpendicular axis passing through one end is ${I}_{1}$. The same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia~about a diameter is ${I}_{2}$. If $\dfrac{I1}{I2}$ is $\dfrac{x{π}^{2}}{3}$, then the value of $x$ will be ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of rod rotating about an axis passing through one end is& ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{ml^{2}}{3} ⋯ \left(1\right)$~

Moment of inertia of ring rotating about one of its diameters is~${I}_{2} = $\dfrac{mR^{2}}{2}.

Since the rod is bent into a ring, the circumference of the ring and the length of the rod are equal,~$l = 2\piR$

Then,~${I}_{2} = $\dfrac{mR^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{ml^{2}}{8{π}^{2}}~

Thus, the ratio~\dfrac{I1}{I2} = \dfrac{8{π}^{2}}{3},so~$x = 8.

$

questions.q: A pulley of radius $1 . 5m$ is rotated about its axis by a force $F = \left(12t - 3t^{2}\right)N$ applied tangentially (while $t$ is measured in seconds). If moment of inertia of the pulley about its axis of rotation is $4 . 5kgm^{2}$, the number of rotations made by the pulley before its direction of motion is reversed, will be $\dfrac{K}{π}$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque of pulley about its axis is& $τ = I\alpha$, where,~$I$~is moment of inertia and~$\alpha$~is angular acceleration.

Torque of a force about its axis is~$τ = FR$, here,~$R$~is radius of pulley.

Then,~\left(12t - 3t^{2}\right)1 . 5 = 4 . 5\alpha$~

$⇒ \alpha = 4t - t^{2}$~

Angular acceleration in terms of angular velocity is

~$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{d \omega}{d t} = 4t - t^{2}$

$⇒ \omega = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(4t - t^{2}\right) d t$

$⇒ \omega = 2t^{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3}$

For $\omega = 0, 2t^{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3} = 0 ⇒ t^{2}\left(2 - \dfrac{t}{3}\right) = 0$

~$⇒ t = 0\text{or}6s$

Now, using~$\omega = \dfrac{d \theta}{d t}$, we have

$\dfrac{d \theta}{d t} = 2t^{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3} ⇒ \theta = {∫}_{0}^{6}\left(2t^{2} - \dfrac{t3}{3}\right) d t$

$= {\dfrac{2t^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{t4}{12}}_{0}^{6}$~

$= {6}^{3}\left(\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{6}{12}\right) = {6}^{3}\left(\dfrac{8 - 6}{12}\right)= \dfrac{63}{6} = 36$

Number~of revolutions $= \dfrac{36}{2\pi} = \dfrac{18}{π}$

$∴ K = 18$

$

questions.q: A thin rod of mass& $0 . 9kg$ and length~$1m$ is suspended, at rest, from one end so that it can freely oscillate in the vertical plane. A particle of move~$0 . 1kg$ moving in a straight line with velocity~$80ms^{- 1}$ hits the rod at its bottom most point and sticks to it (see figure). The angular speed (in $rads^{- 1}$) of the rod immediately after the collision will be …………
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Mass of the rod, $M = 0 . 9kg$

Mass of particle,~$m = 0 . 1kg$

Length of the rod,~$l = 1m$

Velocity of particle,~$v = 80ms^{- 1}$

No external torque acting on the system of rod and particle, so angular momentum of system~about the suspension is conserved, i.e.;~${L}_{i} = {L}_{f}$

$⇒ mvl = I\omega . . . ( 1 )$

Where,~$I$~is the momentum of inertia of rod and particle system,~$\omega$~is the angular velocity of system just after the collision.

$⇒ mvl = \left(\dfrac{Ml^{2}}{3} + ml^{2}\right)\omega . . . ( 2 )$

Substitute the values in equation (2)

$⇒ 0 . 1 \times 80 \times 1 = \left(\dfrac{0 . 9 \times ( 1{)}^{2}}{3} + 0 . 1 \times ( 1{)}^{2}\right) \times \omega$

$\omega = 20rads^{- 1}$

questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $1$ kg rolls without slipping on a plane surface. Its kinetic energy is $7 \times {10}^{- 3}J$. The speed of the centre of mass of the sphere is ______ $cms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let velocity of centre of mass of sphere be& $v$.

Total kinetic energy of solid sphere is~$KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$, where,~$I$~is~moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the axis passing through it's~centre of mass and~$\omega = \dfrac{v}{R} \left(\text{pure rolling condition}\right).

Therefore,

~$7 $\times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times$1 $\times ($v{)}^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{2} \left[\dfrac{2}{5} (1 ) R^{2}\right]\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)2$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}v^{2}\left(\dfrac{7}{5}\right) =7 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ v^{2} = {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ v = {10}^{- 1} = 0 . 1ms^{- 1} = 10cms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Four particles, each of mass $1$ kg are placed at four corners of a square of side $2m$. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is ______kgm^{2}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the moment of inertia of a system of particles about a point can be written as

$I = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{m}_{i}{r}_i^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, ${m}_{i}$ is the mass of the $i^{th}$ particle situated at a distance ${r}_{i}$ from the point.

With reference to the above diagram, it can be written that the net moment of inertia of the system of particles is

$\begin{cases}I & = & ma^{2} + ma^{2} + m ( \sqrt{2}a{)}^{2} \\ & = & 4ma^{2} \\ & = & 4 \times1kg \times \left(2m\right)2 \\ & = & 16kgm^{2}\end{cases}$

questions.q:
A $2$ kg steel rod of length $0 . 6m$ is clamped on a table vertically at its lower end and is free to rotate in the vertical plane. The upper end is pushed so that the rod falls under gravity. Ignoring the friction due to clamping at its lower end, the speed of the free end of the rod when it passes through its lowest position is _______ms^{- 1} .$
(Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2} )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In the above case the torque due to weight of the rod, here use the concept of translation work done and rotational kinetic energy,&

$⇒ W = K . E . ⇒ mgl = \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$, now the moment of inertia of the rod when the axis of rotation passes through one end of the rod,~$I = \dfrac{1 \times ml^{2}}{3}$,
$⇒ mgl = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{ml^{2}}{3}{ω}^{2}$
$⇒ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{6g}{l}}$, now use the relation between linear velocity and angular velocity,~
$⇒ v = l\omega = \sqrt{3 . 6g} = 6ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Consider a disc of mass $5$ kg, radius $2m$, rotating with angular velocity of $10rads^{- 1}$ about an axis perpendicular to the plane of rotation. An identical disc is kept gently over the rotating disc along the same axis. The energy dissipated so that both the discs continue to rotate together without slipping is _________J.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial angular momentum, ${L}_{i} = I{ω}_{i} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2} \cdot \omega = 100kgm^{2}s^{- 1}$

Initial kinetic energy, ${E}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2} \cdot {ω}^{2} = 500J$

From conservation of angular momentum, we can write

$\overset{→}{L}i = \overset{→}{L}f ⇒ 100 = 2I{ω}_{f}$

$⇒ {ω}_{f} = 5rads^{- 1}$

${E}_{f} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{5 ( 2{)}^{2}}{2} \cdot ( 5{)}^{2} = 250J$

Therefore, required energy loss $\Delta E = 250J$

An identical disc is kept gently over the rotating disc along the same axis. The energy dissipated so that both the discs continue to rotate together without slipping is _________J.

questions.q: Two bodies, a ring and a solid cylinder of same material are rolling down without slipping an inclined plane. The radii of the bodies are same. The ratio of velocity of the centre of mass at the bottom of the inclined plane of the ring to that of the cylinder is $\dfrac{x}{2} .$ Then, the value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In both, cases is about point of contact ring,

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2mR^{2}\right){V}_R^{2}R^{2}$

${V}_{R} = \sqrt{gh}$

Solid cylinder

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}mR^{2}\right){v}_C^{2}R^{2}$

${v}_{C} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}$

$\dfrac{vR}{vC} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q:
The moment of inertia of a solid disc rotating along its diameter is 2.5 times higher than the moment of inertia of a ring rotating in similar way. The moment of inertia of a solid sphere which has same radius as the disc and rotating in similar way, is $n$ times higher than the moment of inertia of the given ring. Here, $\mathrm{n}=$ _________.
Consider all the bodies have equal masses.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{MR}_1^2}{4}, $\mathrm{I}$_2=\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}, $\mathrm{I}$_3=\frac{2 \mathrm{MR}_1^2}{5}$ According to problem $\frac{$\mathrm{I}$_1}{$\mathrm{I}$_2}=2.5 \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_1^2}{4}}{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}}=\frac{5}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{R}_1^2}{\mathrm{R}_2^2}=5 \ldots$ Now we are provided with information that $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{I}_3}{\mathrm{I}_2}=\mathrm{n} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{2 \mathrm{MR}_1^2}{5}}{\frac{\mathrm{MR}_2^2}{2}}=\mathrm{n} \Rightarrow \frac{4 \mathrm{R}_1^2}{5 \mathrm{R}_2^2}=\mathrm{n} \end{aligned}$ From Eq', (1) and (2) $\Rightarrow n=4$

questions.q: A person of $80$ kg mass is standing on the rim of a circular platform of mass $200$ kg rotating about its axis at~$5$ revolutions per minute (rpm). The person now starts moving towards the centre of the platform. What will be the rotational speed (in $r$ pm ) of the platform when the person reaches its centre....
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying conservation of angular momentum,

\left({mR}^{2} + \dfrac{MR2}{2}\right)\omega = \dfrac{MR2}{2}\omega '$

\left(80 + \dfrac{200}{2}\right) \times 5 = \dfrac{200}{2}\omega '$

$\omega ' = 9rev / sec .$

questions.q: A circular disc of mass $\text{M}$ and radius $\text{R}$ is rotating about its axis with angular speed ${ω}_{1}$. If another stationary disc having radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and same mass $\text{M}$ is dropped co-axially on to the rotating disc. Gradually both discs attain constant angular speed ${ω}_{2}$. The energy lost in the process is $\text{p%}$ of the initial energy. Value of $p$ is ______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${I}_{1}{ω}_{1} + {I}_{2}{ω}_{2} = \left({I}_{1} + {I}_{2}\right) \times {ω}_{f}$

~

$\dfrac{MR2}{2} \times \omega + 0\left(\dfrac{MR2}{2} + \dfrac{MR2}{8}\right)\dfrac{16}{25}$

${ω}_{f} = \dfrac{4}{5}\omega$

Final~$K . E$.,~${K}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{MR2}{2} + \dfrac{MR2}{8}\right)\dfrac{16}{25}{ω}^{2}$

${K}_{f} = \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{ω}^{2}}{5}$~;~${K}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{MR2}{2}\right){ω}^{2} = \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{ω}^{2}}{4}$

Percentage loss in kinetic energy~$% loss = \dfrac{\dfrac{{MR}^{2}{ω}^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{{MR}^{2}{ω}^{2}}{5}}{{MR}^{2}{ω}^{2}4} \times 100 = 20 %$

questions.q: A solid sphere and a solid cylinder of same mass and radius are rolling on a horizontal surface without slipping. The ratio of their radius of gyrations respectively  \left({k}_{sph}: {k}_{cyl}\right)$ is $2: \sqrt{x}$. The value of $x$ is _______.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering rotational axis as the diametrical axis for sphere and axis of cylinder. Then

${K}_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{2}{5}R^{2}$~and~${K}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}R^{2}$

$∴ \dfrac{K1}{K2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 / 5}{1 / 2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{5}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{K1}{K2} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Comparing it with the given value in the question,

$\dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{2}{x}$

$∴$~$x = 5$

questions.q: For rolling spherical shell, the ratio of rotational kinetic energy and total kinetic energy is $\dfrac{x}{5}$.~The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The rotational kinetic energy is given by&

${K}_{rot} = \dfrac{I{ω}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{3}MR^{2}{ω}^{2}$.

The total kinetic energy is given by~

${K}_{tot} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}MR^{2}{ω}^{2} = \dfrac{mR^{2}{ω}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}MR^{2}{ω}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{6}MR^{2}{ω}^{2}$

Thus, the ratio is~

$\dfrac{Krot}{Ktot} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}MR^{2}{ω}^{2}}{\dfrac{5}{6}MR^{2}{ω}^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Comparing with the given value,

$\dfrac{x}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5} ⇒ x = 2$

questions.q: Four identical discs each of mass '$M$' and diameter '$a$' are arranged in a small plane as shown in figure. If the moment of inertia of the system about $OO^{'}$ is $\dfrac{x}{4}Ma^{2}$. Then, the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering four identical discs as& $1, 2, 3$~and~$4$.

Moment of inertia of disc about diagonal is~${I}_{1} = {I}_{3} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{4}$

Now using~parallel axis theorem,~

Moment of inertia of disc~$2$~and~$4$~is~

${I}_{2} = {I}_{4} = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{4} + MR^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}MR^{2}$

So, net moment of inertia about~$OO^{'}$~is~

~$I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + {I}_{3} + {I}_{4}$

$= 2 $\left(\dfrac{MR^{2}}{4}) +$2 $\left(\dfrac{5}{4}MR^{2})$

~$= \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2}MR^{2}= 3MR^{2}$

Putting $R = \dfrac{a}{2}$

$I = \dfrac{3Ma^{2}}{4},$~so,$x = 3$

$

questions.q:
The angular speed of truck wheel is increased from $900$ rpm to $2460$ rpm in $26$ seconds. The number of revolutions by the truck engine during this time is ______.

(Assuming the acceleration to be uniform).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know,& $\theta = \left(\dfrac{{ω}_{1} + {ω}_{2}}{2}\right)t$

Let number of revolutions be $N$

$∴ 2\piN = 2\pi\left(\dfrac{900 + 2460}{60 \times 2}\right) \times 26$

$N = 728$
